author: mark
text:
v0.3 built-in tool: bash

Adds the `lernie tool bash` subcommand that runs `sh -c <command>` and
returns its stdout per the §3.3 stdio contract. The shell is spawned
in its own process group so a SIGTERM the harness sends to
`lernie tool bash` cascades to every descendant the shell forked
(§2.9). Schema lives at `schemas/tools/bash.json` and the SKILL.md at
`skills/bash/SKILL.md`; the tool dispatcher gains a `bash` arm
alongside the existing `read_file` route.

Cancellation: an internal SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL grace
(`CASCADE_DEADLINE = 2s`) fits inside the 5s outer deadline pinned by
§3.3, so the executor's outer SIGKILL never has to do the teardown.
The cascade is exercised by three unit tests — leaf kill, descendant
kill, and trapped-SIGTERM escalation to SIGKILL.

`tarpaulin.toml` pins `--test-threads=1`: the cascade tests deliver
SIGTERM/SIGKILL to spawned process groups, and the workspace-mode
LLVM engine races against parallel teardown. Serial execution
sidesteps the race; the 100% coverage floor is unchanged.
